title: 美日联手救日元：却卖欧元看多，为何不用美元？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: Cameron, a lot to unpick here. For one, it's not exactly like there was a lot of volatility to step in. The sell-off had been quite orderly. And two, the US decides to do this in euros.
segments.zh: 卡梅伦，这里有很多值得解读的地方。首先，市场波动并不大，抛售也相当有序。其次，美国决定用欧元来干预。

segments.en: What do you make of this joint intervention? Yeah, I think it says it's more about the level of the end than the rate of change.
segments.zh: 你对这次联合干预怎么看？我认为这更多是关于汇率水平，而不是变化速度。

segments.en: Normally, the rate of change is a primary consideration, but we got as high as what? 164 or something.
segments.zh: 通常，变化速度是首要考虑因素，但我们最高到了多少？164左右。

segments.en: In Dalian, the other week. And that's, I mean, you're talking 30 plus year, I mean, 40 plus year,
segments.zh: 在大连，前几周。那是30多年，甚至40多年来的高点。

segments.en: your highs. For a country like the US that's trying to narrow its trade deficit, that makes it quite difficult. And for Japan, that is struggling with an inflation problem,
segments.zh: 对于像美国这样试图缩小贸易逆差的国家来说，这相当困难。而对于正面临通胀问题的日本来说，

segments.en: is struggling with the problem of how to manage the long end of its government bond curve, given the impact of the currency on inflation, it kind of makes sense in that regard.
segments.zh: 考虑到货币对通胀的影响，日本在管理其长期国债收益率曲线方面也面临挑战，从这个角度看，干预是有道理的。

segments.en: Now, why the US has done euros is an interesting question. And I'll be honest, I'm not really sure why they've decided to do that, because it's not like the euro is massively out of line
segments.zh: 现在，为什么美国选择用欧元干预是个有趣的问题。老实说，我不太确定他们为什么这么做，因为欧元并没有大幅偏离。

segments.en: in either direction. So it would have seemed to have made more sense, I think, for the US to have sold dollars, because after all, the US has a dollar printing press.
segments.zh: 所以，我认为美国卖出美元似乎更合理，毕竟美国有印钞机。
